title: Export manifests with sequence IDs and a repair-runner CLI to remediate partial proration/duplicate invoice lines
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem: We still observe intermittent duplicated invoice lines in NetSuite and Stripe when downstream webhook retries overlap with an in-flight mid-cycle plan change or late rate-limit credit backfill. Root cause analysis shows: (1) export jobs are not globally ordered, (2) partial exports (export of usage then export of credits) can be reordered across retries, and (3) downstream systems create new line identifiers instead of merging when the export lacks an authoritative manifest. This leads to proration mismatches and manual accounting adjustments.

Goal: Produce a deterministic, idempotent export surface by emitting a compact export manifest per billing-run with a monotonic sequence ID + per-customer export checksums, and ship a repair-runner CLI/service that can safely reconcile and patch Stripe/NetSuite lines when a mismatch is detected. The manifest enables downstream dedup/merge logic and allows us to detect partial or out-of-order application.

Scope: implement manifest generator in the export pipeline, persist manifest metadata with each export run, extend the export consumer to include manifest metadata in webhook payloads, add manifest-based dedupe in the NetSuite/Stripe adapters, and deliver a repair-runner that can: verify manifests against exported invoice lines, compute corrective patches, and push idempotent amend operations to Stripe and NetSuite with audit trail links.
acceptance_criteria: Each billing export run emits a signed manifest with: run_sequence (monotonic), run_id (uuid), customerChecksum (sha256), and list of line_ids intended
Downstream Stripe/NetSuite adapters reject duplicate export lines when manifest+run_sequence already applied and return a distinct export status code for 'manifest-duplicate', recorded in export logs

Repair-runner can reconcile a mismatched invoice: it compares manifest vs applied lines, produces a deterministic patch plan (add/update/remove), and applies changes idempotently without generating duplicate credits
Automated integration test simulates webhook retry and partial ordering; result is single authoritative invoice in Stripe and matching NetSuite lines
Telemetry: exporter emits metrics for manifest generation time, manifest apply success rate, and repair-runner invocation counts; on-call runbook updated
No change to public billing schema required; downstream consumers get manifest in existing webhook envelope field 'export_metadata'
tasks: Design schema for compact export manifest and sign/encrypt strategy (link to design doc)
Implement manifest generation in billing-export-service and persist to export_store
Add sequence number allocator to leader election path to guarantee monotonic run_sequence
Patch webhook envelope to include export_metadata.manifest_id and signature
Extend stripe-adapter to check manifest before creating invoice lines
Extend netsuite-adapter to dedupe and merge lines using manifest checksums and keep audit reference
Build repair-runner CLI + background job with dry-run mode and rate-limited apply
Add integration tests and chaos test simulating retries and partial exports
Update docs and runbook with remediation steps and escalation flow
tech_decisions: Use monotonic run_sequence as 64-bit integer allocated by export leader to avoid clock skew reliance
Manifests will be signed using service KMS key; downstream will verify signature before applying
We will store only compact manifests (run_id, run_sequence, customerChecksum, line_digest_list) in export_store retention 90 days
Repair-runner will operate in 'dry-run' by default and require a --force flag and an audit ticket for live applies
Adapters will return HTTP 409 with body {error: 'manifest-duplicate'} for duplicate manifests so exporter can mark success instead of retrying
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag manifest emission in staging; 2) Deploy export-store + signer; 3) Roll exporters (staged region) with manifest on and adapters behind feature flag; 4) Run integration tests; 5) Enable adapters globally; 6) Run repair-runner in dry-run across last 30 days of exports and produce reconciliation report; 7) For confirmed mismatches, run repair-runner with --force during a maintenance window. Postmortem follow-up and SLO updates.
